title: Adaptive read-skip scan planner for mixed-OLAP dashboard queries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Dashboard queries that span mixed time resolutions and ad-hoc filters are showing high 95th/99th latency due to full-segment scans and expensive cursor pagination. This ticket implements an adaptive read-skip scan planner that samples index summaries, applies per-tenant bloom/skip filters, and issues targeted partial reads with limited overscan. Goal is to reduce tail latency for large-range queries while preserving throughput and correctness for cursor-based pagination and rollups.
acceptance_criteria: 95th latency for large-range >1M-row tenant queries reduced by >=40% in staging
Average additional I/O for common queries increases by <10% compared to baseline
Cursor pagination correctness verified across random time-window + sorting combos
End-to-end console query tests passing with adaptive planner enabled
Feature gated behind a runtime flag and decoupled from KV cache eviction policy
implementation_notes: Design an index summary sampler that maintains per-shard histograms for timestamp and user_id cardinality
Compute lightweight bloom/skip hints from summaries and persist as small sidecar files for hot shards
Planner stages: 1) index-sample, 2) candidate-segment scoring, 3) selective read with bounded overscan, 4) local mini-aggregate to satisfy top-k/pagination window
Integrate with existing cursor protocol by returning stable continuation tokens that encode skipped offsets and shard-version
Fallback mode: when index summaries are stale or sampling confidence < threshold, revert to current scan path to maintain correctness
Expose runtime flags: enable_adaptive_planner, sampler_confidence_threshold, overscan_limit_ms
Telemetry: emit planner_decision, skipped_bytes, overscan_bytes, sample_confidence, planner_latency metrics to console telemetry pipeline
progress_updates: 2025-03-10 - Spike completed: profiled 50 tenant queries, identified hotspots in late-window scans; sampling reduces candidate segments by ~70% in synthetic tests
2025-03-12 - Prototype planner implemented in staging: can generate candidate segment list and perform selective reads; basic cursor token plumbing added
2025-03-14 - Integration with KV cache reviewed; discovered alignment issue between cached prefix offsets and planner skip hints (added a normalization step)
2025-03-16 - Running A/B on staging with 10% traffic: median unaffected, 95th reduced by 30% on a small set of tenants; noticed increased variance when sketches for certain shards were stale
2025-03-18 - Added decay policy for index summaries and a freshness validator; preparing PR for initial code review
design_decisions: Prefer small, fast index summaries over expensive perfect secondary indexes—trade correctness for fewer reads but maintain deterministic fallback
Use probabilistic skip filters (bloom + min-max ranges) to reduce reads; accept false positives but bound by overscan to avoid correctness regressions
Encode planner state in continuation tokens rather than server-side session to keep planner stateless and sharding-friendly
Keep planner feature-gated and gradually ramp by tenant and by query shape to monitor cost and UX impact
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: stale summaries lead to missed results or large overscan. Mitigation: freshness validator and conservative overscan fallback with correctness-first behavior
Risk: added CPU during candidate scoring might hurt throughput. Mitigation: offload sampling/summary maintenance to background worker and cache recent planner decisions for hot queries
Risk: complexity in cursor tokens across rollouts. Mitigation: token versioning and graceful degradation to legacy cursor when versions mismatch
review_feedback: PM (Lina Morales): request to add SLA check and explicit customer-facing fallback messaging in Console when planner triggers
Design (Arjun Rao): ensure token encoding does not leak tenant identifiers and remains compatible with RBAC audit logs
Eng (Sofia Martinez): prefer having a single telemetry tag 'planner_variant' to correlate with query traces in tracing system
testing_plan: Unit tests for sampler and bloom/skip filter correctness
Property tests comparing planner results with full-scan results over randomized data
Staging A/B with synthetic tenants covering heavy time-range scans and high-cardinality filters
Chaos run: simulate summary staleness and verify fallback correctness
Load test for CPU/IO impact with planner enabled at 100% traffic in a controlled environment
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - feature flagged deploy to staging and run e2e tests
Phase 1 - enable for 5% of production tenants (low traffic) and monitor planner telemetry for 72 hours
Phase 2 - expand to 25% and add throttling knobs if overscan bytes exceed threshold
Phase 3 - enable by default for all tenants behind a conservative overscan limit; implement opt-out in tenant settings
notes: We should coordinate with the Dedicated infra team before enabling planner at scale due to possible IO pattern shifts on GPU-backed hosts.
Consider adding a small on-disk bloom sidecar per shard to persist hints across restarts and reduce warm-up variance.
Follow-up ticket: track impact of planner on billing estimates for customers that self-report token/I/O usage
